optics.source: Warm-amber blinder strip across the centre of a honeycomb lens, with the rest of the face LED

notes: The tower fixture in CBU Room 138, from a photograph of the real stands: a round par with a honeycomb lens, a horizontal warm-amber blinder strip across the middle and LED behind the rest of the face, six to a vertical stand on a weighted base. No manufacturer mark is legible in the photo, so the footprint below is the contract (WW blinder, then R/G/B for the surround) and the physical numbers are read off the picture against the 7-inch-par-sized bodies. Replace with a real profile if the model is identified. Power and beam angle are the two numbers that decide how much of the room one of these fills, and there are twenty-four of them in a 48 x 35 ft space: at 60 W and 60 degrees they washed the whole room flat with no contrast left. 30 W at 40 degrees is a small six-LED par of this size and leaves the beams reading as beams.
